name: self-fallback
description: An expression that falls back to ITSELF: `user?.id || user?.id`. It cannot differ from what it falls back from, so the operator is dead — and the shape is the visible SIGNATURE of a collapsed fallback. Every one of these was born as `user?.id || user?.claims?.sub` in the Replit-OIDC era; the Clerk migration removed the second source and left the operator behind. That collapse was correct, but nothing announced it, and the same codemod applied to a fallback that still mattered would have silently dropped a real alternative. This ratchet exists so the next one is loud. The residual population is behaviourally inert (`v || v === v` for every v) and is NOT worth churning 70 files to remove; what matters is that the count may only go DOWN.
lastBumpNote: 135 -> 134 on 2026-11-07 (W2-TEAM): `req.organization || req.organization` in the deleted analytics team-leaderboard route; measured with npm run lint:ratchets on the rebased tree (main 0abcce71 measured 135).
minimaNote: VACUITY FLOOR on the SCAN POPULATION, not a ratchet. baselineCount above counts BAD THINGS FOUND, so a scan that stops seeing files finds zero and reports it as progress: a zero baseline PASSes on an empty file set, and a nonzero one prints a stale-high "lock it in" for a number that was never true. MEASURED 2026-08-16: this config matched 2402 file(s) (server/**, client/src/**, shared/** minus tests). Floor set to 1900, comfortably below that, so a broken glob or walk trips it while ordinary deletion does not. Checked BEFORE the baseline comparison by scripts/ratchet.mjs; a MISSING floor fails as loudly as a breached one. If a real deletion wave shrinks this population, lower the floor in the same commit and name the wave here — never raise it to silence something, never delete the key. Re-measure with `node scripts/ratchet.mjs --measure`.
